Marissa / Karthik — forwarding HelioPath's ask. Key points: 24 mo EA, asks 45% first-year discount + onboarding credit, regulated PHI use, Private deployment required. Attachments in Diane's note.

My read: good strategic account for healthcare vertical (deep clinical partnerships) and they will bring reference credibility. Economics are material — list ARR would be ~ $1.2M ARR year 1 on current forecast. They want an aggressive upfront concession.

Proposed internal counter (to present as a path forward):
- Offer 30% discount off list for first 12 months, with step-down to 20% year 2;
- Provide up to $50k onboarding credit (one-time) if they commit to the 24-month term and 12-month minimum usage floor (to protect unit economics);
- Add a clause for quarterly usage reviews and automatic reversion to standard rates if monthly usage drops below floor for 2 consecutive quarters.

Requesting: 1) Marissa — do you endorse presenting this compromise to Diane? 2) Jonas — can finance model the expected blended margin and confirm that 30% + $50k credit with the usage floor keeps unit margin above our threshold? 3) If finance pushes back, we will need VP/CFO escalation for the extra delta.

Thanks — I can join a quick call with HelioPath if you want a joint ask.

Naomi
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Naomi / Marissa — ran the numbers. Assumptions we used:
- Forecasted average monthly tokens: 3.2M in months 1–6, ramp 40% by month 12;
- List price per 1k tokens assumed per current rate card;
- Private deployment incremental cost (ops + reserved GPU capacity) accounted for.

Findings:
- 45% discount would reduce gross margin below our minimum threshold even with a $50k credit;
- 30% discount + $50k onboarding credit yields an acceptable blended margin only if HelioPath agrees to a 12-month minimum usage floor equal to 75% of their projected monthly usage for year 1, and an up-front first-quarter prepayment covering at least 25% of year-1 ARR;
- If they accept those guardrails we project positive contribution after fixed infra costs.

Ask for Finance approval path:
- Rafael: recommend we approve up to 35% discount on a case-by-case basis with the guardrails above; anything >35% needs CFO sign-off and executive sponsorship.

I attached a quick P&L scenario (internal). If Marissa/Naomi agree on the guardrails, I'll prepare a one-page memo for Rafael to sign.

Jonas Weber
Head of FP&A
